steps.title: Import acorn and acorn-walk for AST parsing
steps.instruction: Import the acorn parser and acorn-walk traversal utilities from their respective packages.
steps.hint: You'll need two import statements: one for 'acorn' and another for 'acorn-walk'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The acorn parser and acorn-walk utilities are imported and available for use.
successCriteria: Both acorn and acorn-walk are imported from their respective packages.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the AST parsing tools needed for this lesson.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've imported both acorn and acorn-walk.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're importing both acorn and acorn-walk from their packages.

steps.title: Create the main highlightCode function
steps.instruction: Define a function named highlightCode that takes a single parameter called sourceCode.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. The function should be defined in the global scope.
steps.seedCode:
// Import acorn and acorn-walk here

// Define highlightCode function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A highlightCode function is defined with sourceCode as its parameter.
successCriteria: The highlightCode function is defined with the correct name and parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the highlightCode function with the sourceCode parameter.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the function is named exactly 'highlightCode' and takes one parameter called 'sourceCode'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The highlightCode function isn't defined correctly. Check that you used the exact name 'highlightCode' and included the 'sourceCode' parameter.

steps.title: Initialize an empty result array
steps.instruction: Inside your highlightCode function, create an empty array variable called 'result' to store highlighted code segments.
steps.hint: Declare a variable with 'const' and assign it an empty array [].
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating an empty array
const items = [];
steps.expectedOutcome: The highlightCode function will have an empty array variable ready to collect highlighted segments.
successCriteria: An empty array variable named 'result' is declared inside the highlightCode function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created an empty array to store highlighted code segments.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've declared an empty array variable named 'result' inside the highlightCode function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires creating an empty array variable named 'result' inside the highlightCode function. Try again.

steps.title: Parse the source code into an AST
steps.instruction: Inside the highlightCode function, parse the input code string into an AST using acorn.parse(). Store the result in a variable named ast.
steps.hint: Call acorn.parse() with the code parameter as the first argument. The parse method returns an AST object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The highlightCode function will now have an AST variable containing the parsed tree structure of the input JavaScript code.
successCriteria: The function contains a variable named ast that stores the result of calling acorn.parse(code).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully parsed the JavaScript code into an AST structure using acorn.parse().
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling acorn.parse() with the code parameter and storing the result in a variable named ast.
steps.feedbackWrong: The code doesn't parse the input into an AST. Remember to use acorn.parse(code) inside the highlightCode function.

steps.title: Define the node visitor function
steps.instruction: Inside the highlightCode function, define a function named 'visitor' that takes two parameters: 'node' and 'type'.
steps.hint: This function will be called for each node in the AST. Use a function declaration or arrow function.
steps.expectedOutcome: A visitor function is defined inside highlightCode, ready to process AST nodes.
successCriteria: The highlightCode function contains a 'visitor' function with 'node' and 'type' parameters.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've defined the visitor function that will process each AST node.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a function named 'visitor' with two parameters: 'node' and 'type'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The visitor function is not correctly defined. It should be inside highlightCode and take 'node' and 'type' parameters.

steps.title: Add string literal handling to visitor
steps.instruction: Inside the node visitor function, add a condition to check if the node type is 'StringLiteral'. When it is, push a span element with the string value into the result array.
steps.hint: Use an if statement to check node.type === 'StringLiteral'. Then use result.push() with a string like `${node.value}`.
steps.expectedOutcome: The visitor function will now detect string literals and wrap them in span tags for highlighting.
successCriteria: The visitor function contains an if statement that checks for 'StringLiteral' nodes and pushes a span element with the node's value into the result array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added string literal handling to the visitor function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your condition checks node.type === 'StringLiteral' and pushes the correct span element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The visitor function doesn't yet handle string literals. Add an if statement for 'StringLiteral' nodes that pushes a span element.

steps.title: Add numeric literal handling to visitor
steps.instruction: Inside the visitor function, add an else-if condition to detect NumericLiteral nodes and wrap their value with a span tag with class 'number'.
steps.hint: Check if node.type equals 'NumericLiteral'. If it does, push a span element with class 'number' containing the node.value into the result array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The visitor function will now wrap numeric values (like 42 or 3.14) with <span class="number"> tags.
successCriteria: The visitor function includes an else-if condition for NumericLiteral nodes that pushes a span with class 'number' containing the node.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added handling for numeric literals. The visitor now recognizes numbers in the code and wraps them for highlighting.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're checking for 'NumericLiteral' type and pushing the correct HTML string with the node.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The visitor function doesn't yet handle numeric literals. Add an else-if condition for node.type === 'NumericLiteral' that pushes a span with class 'number'.

steps.title: Add keyword handling to visitor
steps.instruction: Inside the visitor function, add an else-if condition to check if node.type is 'Identifier' and if node.name matches common JavaScript keywords like 'function', 'return', or 'if'. If it does, push a span with class 'keyword' containing the node.name to the result array.
steps.hint: You can create an array of keyword strings and check if node.name is included in that array. Then wrap the node.name in a span with class 'keyword' and push it to result.
steps.expectedOutcome: The visitor function will now detect JavaScript keywords and wrap them in span tags with the 'keyword' class.
successCriteria: The visitor function includes an else-if condition that checks for 'Identifier' nodes with names matching keywords and pushes a span with class 'keyword' to the result array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added keyword detection to the visitor function. This will highlight JavaScript keywords in the code.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some keyword handling, but make sure you're checking for 'Identifier' nodes and matching specific keyword names like 'function', 'return', or 'if'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The keyword handling logic is missing or incorrect. Ensure you add an else-if condition for 'Identifier' nodes and check if node.name is a keyword before pushing a span.

steps.title: Traverse the AST with the visitor
steps.instruction: Inside the highlightCode function, after defining the visitor function, call acornWalk.simple() to traverse the AST using your visitor.
steps.hint: Use acornWalk.simple(ast, visitor) to walk through all nodes in the AST.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AST will be walked through completely, allowing the visitor to process each node.
successCriteria: acornWalk.simple() is called with the AST and visitor function as arguments.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the AST traversal. The visitor will now process every node in the parsed tree.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling acornWalk.simple() with both the AST and your visitor function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AST traversal isn't set up yet. You need to call acornWalk.simple(ast, visitor) to walk through the entire AST structure.

steps.title: Create the HTML output structure
steps.instruction: Inside the highlightCode function, after the AST traversal, create and return a div element containing a pre element. The pre element should have the result array joined into a single string as its inner HTML.
steps.hint: You can use template literals to create the HTML string. The div should wrap a pre tag, and the pre's content should be the joined result array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The highlightCode function will now return a div containing a pre element with the highlighted code as inner HTML.
successCriteria: The highlightCode function returns a div element containing a pre element with the result array joined into a string as its inner HTML.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the HTML output structure for the highlighted code.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the function returns a div containing a pre element with the joined result array as inner HTML.
steps.feedbackWrong: The HTML output structure is not yet correct. Ensure you return a div with a pre element inside, containing the joined result array.

steps.title: Populate the code display with highlighted content
steps.instruction: Inside the highlightCode function, join the result array into a string and return it as the HTML content for the code display.
steps.hint: Use the join method on the result array to combine all the span elements into a single string.
steps.expectedOutcome: The highlightCode function now returns a string of concatenated HTML span elements ready to be inserted into the DOM.
successCriteria: The highlightCode function returns the joined result array as a string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully joined the highlighted segments into a single HTML string. This prepares the content for display.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning the joined string from the highlightCode function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on joining the result array and returning it as a string. Check the hint for guidance.

steps.title: Return the complete highlighted code element
steps.instruction: In the highlightCode function, return the result array joined into a single string to create the final highlighted HTML output.
steps.hint: Use the join method on the result array to combine all the span elements into one string.
steps.expectedOutcome: The highlightCode function now returns the complete highlighted HTML string by joining all the span elements in the result array.
successCriteria: The highlightCode function returns result.join('') to produce the final highlighted code output.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've completed the highlightCode function by returning the joined result array. This creates the final highlighted HTML output from all the processed AST nodes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're returning result.join('') at the end of the highlightCode function to combine all the span elements into a single HTML string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The highlightCode function should return the joined result array. Add 'return result.join('');' at the end of the function to complete it.
